name: Maratha Confederacy

areaKm2.note: Over 2.5 million km2 at the 1760 zenith, about a third of the subcontinent (Turchin, Adams and Hall 2006 p. 223, via the article) (high, includes chauth-paying tributaries); low for the directly ruled swarajya and sardar domains. The world_1715 Maratha polygon (~87,000 km2) is the Shahu-era homeland and badly understates 1760; world_1783 has a "Maratha Confederacy" polygon (~1.05 million km2) but postdates the snapshot.

population.note: About a third of the subcontinent by area (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire); OWID/HYDE India 1750 = 183M, Pakistan 14.9M, Bangladesh 17.1M (~215M, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). One third = ~72M; the Deccan was less dense than the Ganges plain, so mid 60M. High includes tributaries paying chauth.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Pune, Nagpur, Indore, Baroda, Ahmedabad (shared), garrison towns.

activePersonnel.note: The Panipat field army (1760-61) had 55,000 cavalry (11,000 regular) and 9,000 Gardi infantry, while the bulk of the Maratha army stayed in the Deccan with the Peshwa (via the article); over 50,000 regular troops took Delhi in August 1760 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire). Total standing household and silladar horse, infantry and fort garrisons doubled from Panipat.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Pindari irregular horse, local militia, sardar contingents not under arms.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Gunners, artillery train and fleet crews (gallivats and grabs).

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Silladar cavalry raised by contract from Deccan peasant-soldiers.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Silladar and bargir light horse: 44,000 irregular cavalry at Panipat (55,000 minus 11,000 regular, via the article) plus the Deccan, Nagpur and Gujarat armies.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: sword, spear, few firearms; hardy Deccani ponies.

count.note: Paga household regular cavalry: 11,000 at Panipat (via the article) (low).
9,000 Gardi infantry of Ibrahim Khan Gardi, trained in the French manner under Bussy (via the article) (low); plus Arab, Sindhi and Purbiya mercenary musketeers.
Educated guess. Mavala hill infantry and fort garrisons of the Western Ghats.
Almost 150 pieces of modern long-range French-made artillery went north with the Panipat army (via the article) (low); Deccan and fort guns added (educated).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: French-made guns outranging the Afghans.

count.note: Educated guess. Grabs of the Peshwa's fleet after the Angre fleet was destroyed at Vijaydurg (1756).
Educated guess. Gallivats under Anandrao Dhulap (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Navy).

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: Sadashivrao Bhau and Peshwa Balaji Bajirao; brilliant raiding but a confederacy of rival sardars with friction over tactics at Panipat.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: confederacy of Holkar, Scindia, Bhonsle and Gaekwad; Holkar left the field at Panipat.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: Attock reached 1758, Delhi retaken August 1760.

weapons.note: Anchor 5-6: French-pattern muskets and long-range guns with the Gardis; most cavalry with sword and spear.

armor.note: Anchor 4-5: quilted and mail armour, little in use.

ships.note: Anchor 4-5: grabs and gallivats, outclassed by East India Company ships.

fortification.note: Anchor 5: hill forts and sea forts (Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg).

logistics.note: Anchor 4-5: banjara grain carriers and foraging; the Panipat army starved when cut off.

communications.note: Anchor 5 minus: harkara couriers and newsletters.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Chauth and sardeshmukhi were collected by armies; the Peshwa state ran on military debt.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Textiles and crafts; Mughal-era structure (Moosvi's 18% for the 16th century) assumed slightly lower.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Dry Deccan farming; famine-prone.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Mughal highways through Malwa and the Deccan; ghat passes.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Bassein, Kalyan, Kolaba, Vijaydurg, Ratnagiri.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Light horse living off the land raided to Attock and Bengal; heavy armies were tied to supply (Panipat).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, bullocks of banjara carriers, camels.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: hill forts of the Western Ghats, guerrilla tradition that wore down Aurangzeb, local supply.

notes: Snapshot = autumn 1760, Maratha zenith after the recapture of Delhi, before the Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761). Personnel convention: household (paga) and contracted silladar cavalry, Gardi and mercenary infantry and fort garrisons under arms are activePersonnel; pindaris and uncalled sardar contingents are trainedReserves. Panipat figures via the Third Battle of Panipat article (Gordon, Roy); Gommans and Roy on Maratha warfare not consulted directly. Border: the nearest file at or before 1760 is world_1715, whose Maratha polygon is the early homeland only. Population convention: Peshwa domains and the great sardar states (Holkar, Scindia, Bhonsle, Gaekwad) plus chauth-paying tracts in the high value.
